title: One differential descends through the filtered cycle-boundary quotients
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], K an integer-indexed cochain complex, F a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration], and r≥1 an integer. Let j=i+(r,1-r). Form Q_r^a=coker(B_r^a→Z_r^a) using the concrete cycles and boundaries [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] and their inclusion [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundaries-le-cycles], and write π_a:Z_r^a→Q_r^a for its cokernel projection. There exists a single morphism δ:Q_r^i→Q_r^j such that for every object A and maps t,tprime,x,y at i,j, if dt=tprime in K and x,y are the respective graded projections of t,tprime, then x π_i δ=y π_j. This asserts neither square-zero, shape at nonrelated pairs, nor uniqueness.

proof.text: For any simultaneous source and derivative representatives whose source page class is zero, factor the source cycle map through its monic boundary inclusion using Abelian.monoLift. Refine along the epimorphism from boundary representatives to their graded image. The difference from the chosen boundary representative has zero graded projection. Evaluation of the filtration cokernel sequence is exact, so this difference factors through the next filtration step F^(p+1). The ambient boundary representative sum is contained in the inverse image under d of d(F^(p+1)): the incoming differential image maps into this inverse image by the existing private theorem CategoryTheory.image_le_pullback from FilteredComplexBoundariesLECycles (available through a proof-only import all), using d squared = 0; F^(p+1) maps into its image by the image/pullback adjunction. Hence the derivative of the refined representative belongs to d(F^(p+1)). It also belongs to F^(p+r) by the representative equation. Their intersection is the target boundary representative object, since (p+r)-r+1=p+1 and the total degree increases by one. Factor its graded projection through target boundaries, identify the refined target cycle map by monicity, apply the target cokernel condition and cancel the refining epimorphism. This zero-class calculation is fully proved locally and works for all integer r.

Choose the epimorphic family x of simultaneous representatives supplied by the representative-cover theorem. The composite e=x followed by the source boundary cokernel projection is epic. Apply the zero-class calculation to the family precomposed with kernel.ι e; the target page map kills kernel e. Abelian.epiDesc then produces delta on the source page quotient, with e delta equal to the chosen target representative followed by its page projection.

Given any other representative family over a test object B, pull back e along its source page class. The second pullback projection is epic. Subtract the chosen and given representative families after the respective pullback projections. Additivity preserves all three representative equations, and the pullback equation makes the difference source page class zero. Apply the proved zero-class calculation to deduce equality of the two target page classes. Combine this equality with the descent equation and cancel the second pullback projection to obtain the asserted formula over B.

theorem filteredComplex_single_differential_descent
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (F : DecreasingFiltration K) (r : ℤ) (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (i j : ℤ × ℤ) (hij : (ComplexShape.up' (r, 1 - r)).Rel i j) :
    let Q := fun pq : ℤ × ℤ ↦ cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _
      (filteredComplex_boundaries_le_cycles K F pq.1 (pq.1 + pq.2) r))
    let π := fun pq : ℤ × ℤ ↦ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _
      (filteredComplex_boundaries_le_cycles K F pq.1 (pq.1 + pq.2) r))
    ∃ δ : Q i ⟶ Q j,
      ∀ (A : C)
        (t : A ⟶ (F.step i.1 : CochainComplex C ℤ).X (i.1 + i.2))
        (t' : A ⟶ (F.step j.1 : CochainComplex C ℤ).X (j.1 + j.2))
        (x : A ⟶ (F.complexCycles i.1 (i.1 + i.2) r : C))
        (y : A ⟶ (F.complexCycles j.1 (j.1 + j.2) r : C)),
        t ≫ (F.step i.1).arrow.f (i.1 + i.2) ≫ K.d (i.1 + i.2) (j.1 + j.2) =
          t' ≫ (F.step j.1).arrow.f (j.1 + j.2) →
        x ≫ (F.complexCycles i.1 (i.1 + i.2) r).arrow =
          t ≫ (F.complexQuotientπ i.1 (i.1 + 1) (by omega)).f (i.1 + i.2) →
        y ≫ (F.complexCycles j.1 (j.1 + j.2) r).arrow =
          t' ≫ (F.complexQuotientπ j.1 (j.1 + 1) (by omega)).f (j.1 + j.2) →
        x ≫ π i ≫ δ = y ≫ π j
